# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 16 (PNEUMA Dynamic)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 16
**Agent:** PNEUMA (Dynamic)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Now let me also speak to you about the temple — about how those poor, misguided people placed their hope in a building as if it were God's house, instead of in the God who made them.
2. They consecrated him in a temple, practically like the Gentiles do. But what does the Lord say? "Who measured out the sky with the palm of his hand, or the earth with his fist? Was it not I?" says the Lord. "Heaven is my throne and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house are you going to build me? What place will serve as my resting place?" says the Lord. Their hope is clearly empty.
3. And again he says: "Look — the very people who tore this temple down will build it back up."
4. And it is happening. The enemies knocked it down in war, and now those same enemies' servants are going to rebuild it.
5. It was also revealed that the city, the temple, and the people of Israel were all going to be given over to ruin. Scripture says: "And in the last days the Lord will hand over the sheep of the flock — the pen and the watchtower — to destruction." And it happened exactly as the Lord said.
6. So let us ask: is there a temple of God? There is — and here is where he says he makes it and brings it to completion. It is written: "When the week comes to an end, a temple of God will be built in glory in the name of the Lord."
7. I find that there is indeed a temple. But how will it be built in the name of the Lord? Listen: before we believed in God, our hearts were a ruined, rotting dwelling — a house built by human hands, crammed with idols, a home for demons. Everything we did was against God.
8. But it will be built in the name of the Lord. Pay close attention, so that the temple of the Lord may be built with real glory. How? This is how: we received forgiveness of our sins. We put our hope in the Name. We became new people — made again from scratch. And now God truly lives in our dwelling place — in us.
9. How does this work? Through his word of faith, the call of his promise, the wisdom of his righteous commandments, the instructions of his teaching — he himself prophesying within us, he himself living in us. He opened for us who were slaves of death the door of the temple — which is the mouth — and gave us repentance, and brought us into the temple that will never decay.
10. Anyone who wants to be saved does not look at the speaker but at the one who lives in the speaker and speaks through them — marveling that these words were never heard before, never even desired before. This is a spiritual temple being built for the Lord.
